Resident-frame lowering: task-pipeline pays two inert count calls for the two static separator fragments in its final interpolation, plus one extra skipped frame-bookkeeping check. Same-base A/B at 0, 1, 16 and 900000 pipeline items keeps these deltas fixed at +2 calls/+1 skip, with ownership total unchanged at 12318776 for the full benchmark. Fragment controls give +1 call per static text piece and zero calls without text pieces. This bounded per-run work replaces per-await live-row copying; it does not scale with pipeline items or suspension states.

#1809 (e70be2212): decode reads JSON in one pass through the keyed stream reader. Its key loop writes each member into a slot and probes the guess and the per-type name table per key; those take count operations on string keys and slot values that are already sole-owned or static, which the runtime skips. The reader replaces two passes (validate with an index, then read), and decode is 6-21% faster on 10 MB documents (A/B on #1809). #2173 (4b): a body now releases a T? held in locals (Facts.find, a decoded optional) with the inline address count, whose call-site null test skips .None and counts the skip. Before 4b the body called the out-of-line walk helper, whose variant switch skipped .None uncounted. The real call became an inline test: less work, no call added; no-op calls are unchanged.
